content: Memory initialization preserves malformed NDJSON lines; `memory_repair` explicitly removes them on request.
Pi natively enables or disables installed package extensions via `pi config`, with global and project-local resource filters persisted in settings.json.
Shared pi-tools configuration lives in lib/pi-tools-config.ts with defaults < global < trusted-project precedence and is tested by `npm run test:config`.

`extensions/pi-tools-settings.ts` provides registry-driven `/pi-tools` settings and scoped status/get/set/enable/disable commands; its root navigator selects write scope and extensions, detail screens retain that scope, Esc returns to root, and saved edits reload Pi on close.
`npm run format` runs Prettier across the repository; Prettier is a devDependency.

extensions/tool-output-compression/ provides observe-default result profiles, exact reuse, session-scoped raw retrieval, and the /tool-output dashboard; its tests run through npm run test:compression.
Tool-output compression uses a private SQLite store with WAL, synchronous=FULL, 600-permission files, bounded busy retries, retention/quota controls, and session-scoped retrieve_tool_output chunks.
`/tool-output` reports potential savings in observe mode and actual applied exact-reuse savings in apply mode, while `/tool-output prune` and `vacuum` maintain the SQLite store.
The root package declares `"type": "module"`, so Node runs the TypeScript ESM tests without `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` reparsing warnings.

The registered Vitest output profile uses `profiles.test.vitest.mode`, defaults to observe, and strictly compacts only standalone successful file-level or test-level reporter output after durable raw storage.
The registered bash JSON/JSONL profile uses profiles.structured.json.mode, defaults to observe, lexically minifies complete or line-bounded embedded values, and uses session-scoped raw retrieval.
The registered search-records bash profile uses profiles.search.records.mode, defaults to observe, and reversibly groups certified rg/grep opaque prefix:<decimal>:suffix records with raw retrieval.
The custom stats footer measures last and aggregate TPS from assistant message_start-to-message_end stream intervals using final usage.output, so tool execution time is excluded.

The subagents extension publishes enabled, maxConcurrentWorkers (integer, default 2), models.task, and models.research settings and resolves trusted-project launch policy before creating a worker session.

extensions/subagents/supervisor.ts manages injectable persistent SDK worker sessions with retry disabled, atomic manifests and terse journals in tmp/subagents, shared immediate-refusal concurrency, Git observation, and paused interrupted-work recovery.

Task workers use subagent_task_launch, subagent_task_follow_up, and subagent_task_report; each concluded run persists a structured report plus full final response under tmp/subagents/<id>/reports and injects one bounded handoff with a non-context timeline entry.

Task-worker controls are exposed through subagent_task_control: redirect steers a live worker, checkpoint persists bounded recovery metadata, pause aborts resumably, cancel disposes terminally, and explicit resume reopens the saved SDK session after interrupted work is recovered as paused.

Research jobs use subagent_research_launch/report/control with the research model, retain full reports and normalized cited source indexes under tmp/subagents, send one bounded cited handoff, and deliver only that synthesis to an explicitly linked live task worker.

Subagents delegationMode defaults to proactive and injects per-turn main-agent guidance to autonomously launch bounded useful workers; manual disables that guidance, and SDK worker sessions suppress subagent tools and guidance to prevent recursion.
The Subagent workstreams widget displays active or attention-needed workstreams and unconsumed inbox handoffs, with optional event tails; it clears when no rows remain.
memory_remember now carries typed canonical memory details for a TUI renderer that shows stored content while preserving the concise raw tool result and hidden project-memory injection.

Pi ExtensionAPI can block validated individual tool calls via `tool_call` returning `{ block, reason }`, but `before_agent_start`, `turn_end`, and `agent_end` expose no turn-cancellation or required-delegation hook.

Subagent completions persist atomic records under tmp/subagents/completion-inbox, deliver bounded handoffs by steer when the parent is active or nextTurn when idle without triggerTurn, and acknowledge them on matching message_end.

Subagents expose subagent_wait to snapshot selected or all live workers, return bounded terminal inbox handoffs, consume them to prevent deferred duplicate delivery, and leave workers/inbox untouched on cancellation.

Pi preserves the per-turn system prompt override through auto-compaction retries in the same agent run; before_agent_start re-runs on the next top-level prompt, while memory's session_compact handler reinjects its custom context only at that next start.
Pi auto-loads direct `extensions/*.ts`; the pi-tools settings test lives at `tests/pi-tools-settings.test.ts` so its top-level theme initialization is not imported during SDK worker resource loading.
Pi 0.84 passes the active Agent run AbortSignal to every custom tool execution; steering queues input after tool completion and does not abort tools, while Agent.abort aborts that signal.

While main-session subagent_wait is active, interactive/RPC input now aborts the wait, preserves workers and inbox records, and replays captured text/images FIFO after agent settlement via pi.sendUserMessage.
Subagents expose outputTailLines as a non-negative integer setting defaulting to 0 for concise live thinking and tool lifecycle widget tails.

ResearchWorkstreamService writes normalized reports and citation source indexes under tmp/subagents/<workstream>/ after settlement, but its worker brief does not explicitly direct worker-created notes there.
Mason is a Neovim/Lua-specific registry without a documented Node embedding API, so managed LSP provisioning should use a pi-tools-owned reviewed catalog and private versioned installation root.

extensions/lsp-inspection/ provides immutable managed TypeScript/Go/Python catalog descriptors, primitive settings including ensureInstalled, secure agent-owned atomic inventory state, and tests via npm run test:lsp.

extensions/lsp-inspection/provisioner.ts provisions only reviewed npm/go catalog entries through injectable runners, staged atomic promotion, probe/integrity validation, typed availability outcomes, and shared per-catalog in-flight cancellation.
LSP Inspection waits for fresh push diagnostics (including a TypeScript-safe 900ms quiet window), supports dynamic pull registration and diagnostic refresh, and opts gopls into pull diagnostics.

extensions/lsp-inspection/index.ts trust-gates session runtime, publishes LSP settings, manages shared cancellable provisioning with staged private installs and lockfile integrity/probe validation plus a reusable vscode-languageserver-protocol stdio client/server manager, exposes lsp_inspect only for enabled trusted sessions, and cleans up processes and installers on shutdown.
LSP inspection results and tool details carry bounded catalog-specific availability messages, rendering typed provisioning failures for unavailable file and partial workspace diagnostics.
Managed npm LSP installs omit --no-save so npm writes a root package-lock.json; --prefix lock entries may use stage-prefixed package paths.
The root project has no TypeScript compiler configuration; subagent code derives AgentMessage from pi-coding-agent's exported AgentSession to avoid direct nested pi-agent-core type resolution.

Subagent widget visibility is driven by durable manifest status and independent completion-inbox delivery state: needs_decision, blocked, paused, starting, and running manifests remain visible even after inbox acknowledgment or consumption, while report reads only refresh and do not resolve lifecycle status.

Subagent task and research model settings use Pi session scoped-model picker values when available, including pinned thinking levels, while retaining free-form stored pattern compatibility when no scope exists.
In pi-tools settings UI, string settings with selectValues render in a searchable submenu SelectList instead of cycling values.

Subagent launch, resume, and inactive follow-up synchronously reserve shared concurrency slots before setup, count reservations alongside active runs, and release reservations on failure; follow-ups without a limit permit live-only delivery.

Subagents expose thinking.task and thinking.research as inherit-default enums; saved values override model suffixes, absent settings preserve suffixes or inherit parent thinking, and Pi clamps levels when creating worker sessions.
gopls v0.23.0 advertises document pull diagnostics but workspaceDiagnostics=false, so lsp_inspect must use mode='file' with a root-relative .go path for Go diagnostics.
Pyright's pyright-langserver rejects --version without a transport, so LSP provisioning probes the immutable companion node_modules/.bin/pyright executable instead.
LSP Inspection sends gopls only pullDiagnostics initialization options, so gopls v0.23.0 runs its default-enabled modernize passes and lsp_inspect returns their hint diagnostics, such as any.
An already-running Pi session keeps its loaded extension implementation after filesystem edits; restart or reload Pi before retesting changed extension behavior.
LSP Inspection normalizes document and workspace pull reports with empty or omitted kind plus items as full reports, covering gopls v0.23 zero-value JSON.

gopls v0.23 document pull diagnostics analyze the narrowest package configuration, while unusedfunc requires gopls' widest same-package configuration; therefore lsp_inspect file mode misses unused-function diagnostics in packages with in-package _test.go files.
Pi v1.0 codemode runs JavaScript in QuickJS to compose session tools and filter results before model exposure, enabled explicitly with defaultTools: ["+codemode"] or automatically by MCP when needed.

extensions/browser-tools/index.ts registers managed Playwright Chromium sessions on macOS; external tabs use a separate, limited direct page-scoped CDP attachment. Existing Pi processes retain previously loaded tools until reloaded or restarted.

The Playwright browser runtime uses a pinned 1.64.1 Chromium installer with SQLite coordination and durable fail-closed markers; independent testing reproduced a detached child escaping its monitored process group and continuing after the marker was removed. macOS headless/headed tests run via npm run test:browser:live.

Playwright named profiles use private validated directories, durable nonce markers and SQLite leases with process-local arbitration, releasing after confirmed context close and failing closed on ambiguous ownership.

Browser registration wires BrowserDiagnostics into ManagedSessions before navigation, exposes browser_diagnostics and browser_diagnostic_headers, and clears capture on tab/session invalidation; per-page native listeners provide bounded history, credential redaction and scoped reveal, terminal request outcomes, and update-sequence cursors.
Browser inspection stores oversized DOM/eval results in private owner-scoped artifacts with bounded UTF-8 retrieval and export; artifact cleanup is opportunistic and uncertain crashes fail closed.
Browser ArtifactStore supports putBinary(owner, asyncBytes, {maxBytes, signal}) and readBinary raw-byte-offset base64 chunks under the same lock, quota, expiry and export as text artifacts.
browser_download captures owned-page downloads as creator-scoped binary artifacts, and ManagedSessions waits for bounded download cleanup before closing its owned browser.
Browser download history has no small default count cap; large lists use owner-scoped artifacts, while configured admission and retention limits remain explicit.
browser_extract uses owner-scoped serialized page access and private artifacts, and resolves sanitized requested URLs only while the captured main-document loader and navigation epoch match.

Browser downloads publish owner-scoped binary artifacts with bounded retention and explicit unknown cleanup states; research extraction uses isolated-world bounded traversal and verified per-document navigation provenance.

Playwright recording finalizes video-enabled contexts before browser close and publishes verified binary artifacts; native temporary recording bytes are not quota-bounded and recovery discovery is read-only.

Browser diagnostics capture exact-request declared-small uncompressed identity response bodies best-effort using Playwright response.body(), with two global in-flight reads and bounded retained bytes; unsupported responses are explicit and transient browser, transport, and Node memory are not strictly bounded.
browser_snapshot_ref supports bounded normal Playwright clicks on retained snapshot ElementHandles after stale-reference validation, with uncertain failure reporting and no automatic retry.

Browser snapshots and reference validation are owner-scoped and serialized, retaining exact Playwright handles with stale-reference checks; frameSelector targets one main-document iframe and scopes selector inside it. `browser_pick` supports multiple selections and existing child frames in visible owned sessions, cancels on frame changes, returns non-actionable metadata, and quarantines uncertain failures.

browser_action serializes bounded click, fill, select, press, scroll, and wait against retained refs or strict scoped selectors, and reports sampled text, URL, or response verification separately from action completion.

Browser actions wait for unique targets and report uncertain dispatch without replay; browser_screenshot returns direct PNGs and owner-scoped artifacts for viewport, full-page or snapshot-ref element captures and quarantines uncertain captures. browser_viewport sizes owned tabs with configurable screenshot limits.

browser_upload stages explicitly listed regular files from open descriptors to private disk before snapshot-ref or chooser upload; explicit MIME overrides use an in-memory payload. browser_dialog explicitly resolves owned pending dialogs and reports operation status; dialog monitors reconcile ordinary human dismissal without automatic acceptance or replay.

User-approved external browser attachment uses direct selected-page CDP with literal-loopback discovery and cross-process target leases; it supports title, bounded DOM text, HTTP navigation and opt-in diagnostics, not actions, screenshots, uploads, dialogs or recording. Disconnect does not close the external browser.

browser_eval returns an awaiting-dialog handoff for blocking dialogs; browser_dialog refresh reports externally dismissed dialog state as unknown without sending a response and directs owned-session cleanup.

browser_upload supports strict selector or role/name chooser targets, extension-based MIME inference and explicit MIME overrides; final symlinks are rejected while parent symlinks are followed and file bytes are read from opened descriptors.
Browser attachment leases use shared-root durable SQLite profile locks keyed by hashed CDP target ID across endpoint aliases and processes; uncertain active operations quarantine ownership.

Owned Chromium page CDP dialog opening and closed events include frame IDs and cover local and OOPIF fixtures, but consecutive identical dialogs have indistinguishable payloads and enabling Page on an already-open dialog can stall.

Owned browser pages prearm a page-scoped CDP dialog monitor that correlates ordered opening/closing events with Playwright dialogs and frame epochs; disconnects or mismatches leave dialog status unknown.

A disposable Chromium probe showed Playwright connectOverCDP can dismiss a confirm dialog on an unselected external tab; browser-level Playwright attachment is disabled in favor of direct selected-page CDP.

browser_handoff pauses an owned visible session until explicit interactive or RPC confirmation; a headless named-profile session can request a visible restart only with separate user consent, transferring its exclusive profile lease after verified closure before the new paused handoff.
Browser human handoff hides paused-session URLs, discards and suspends session diagnostics until confirmation, and refuses sessions with video or unresolved native tracing.

Human browser handoff suspends DownloadManager without reading, cancelling, or deleting user downloads and keeps capture disabled after confirmation because delayed human download events cannot be reliably attributed.

After browser handoff, owner-scoped browser_download capture_status reports suspended capture and resume_capture requires acknowledgeRisk=true because delayed human downloads may become agent artifacts.

browser_pick multi-selection defaults to 20 and accepts larger positive safe-integer limits; browser-pick-finish ends a batch early, handles are disposed, and bounded non-actionable metadata includes parent context and synthetic summaries with explicit truncation and omission notices, not original HTML or selectors. Snapshot records with incomplete identity never receive actionable references.
Pi 1.4 resolves duplicate extension tool names by extension load order, and getAllTools exposes only the winning definition even when a later extension registers the same name.
The memory store serializes cooperating processes with a project-wide SQLite lock; non-cooperating manual edits can still race file replacement.
Project memory injects full knowledge plus recall guidance, while practices and decisions are retrieved on demand; the briefing refreshes on a new session or after compaction.

Subagents workstreams may retain stale `queued` rows after a completion-inbox record has been pulled or acknowledged; report reads alone do not consume records, and `subagent_wait` snapshots only live workers. The user also wants task rows labeled “Task” rather than “Task worker,” with the latest output line shown beneath the purpose when useful.
Browser extraction and semantic snapshots expose configurable per-call budgets above their defaults; snapshot registration forwards node, character, record, frame, scope and identity budgets.
Browser picker returns complete per-selection bounded metadata inline or in an owner-scoped artifact, and reports quota failure after selection and handle cleanup.

Managed browser navigation, snapshot/action/chooser selectors, role names, prompt input and eval code have no tool-specific length caps; managed action, upload and navigation deadlines are bounded by Node's 2147483647ms timer maximum.

Oversized managed browser action and dialog operation results preserve dispatch status and verification inline and publish full results as owner-scoped artifacts; artifact failures retain explicit dispatch warnings.

Browser screenshot dimension, pixel and PNG-byte settings accept safe integers; viewport sizing is budget-gated, and images exceeding Node's base64 string limit return an explicit artifact-only result.
Screenshot results preserve a published owner-scoped artifact ID when base64 conversion throws a recoverable error, with a sanitized image-omission reason.

Selected-page browser attachment inspection accepts maxNodes and maxChars, traverses read-only DOM in bounded CDP chunks with explicit coverage counts and budget-stop reasons, and stores oversized results in owner-scoped artifacts.
External attached-page inspection runs in a selected-frame CDP isolated world and fails closed on detected navigation or document identity changes between chunks.
External attachment title reads use a selected-frame isolated CDP world and fail closed on navigation or frame loader identity changes.
Browser attachment operations, download waits, and screenshot/viewport deadlines retain their defaults and accept up to Node's 2147483647ms timer maximum.
Project Memory consolidation starts in the foreground through `/memory-review` or `memory_consolidate`; it has no background review scheduler.
SDK subagent worker sessions do not bind the extension lifecycle, so session_start-dependent extensions may not initialize.
